findings.issue_text: CredentialHelper.java:124 leaves previous local recovery codes intact after successfully storing replacements externally, allowing old codes to remain valid through local-provider fallback. Remove the previous local credential when external replacement succeeds.

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 validates recovery codes without persisting consumption, allowing indefinite replay and incorrectly reporting all codes as remaining. Persist consumption and test replay rejection.

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:getCredentials returns a legacy OTP model with unset credentialData and secretData, causing OTP deserialization to fail during account credential listing. Convert it to a modern OTP credential model before returning it.

goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialHelper.java:124 leaves previous local recovery codes intact after successfully storing replacements externally, allowing old codes to remain valid through local-provider fallback. Remove the previous local credential when external replacement succeeds.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the createRecoveryCodesCredential method in CredentialHelper.java (lines 112-129), when userStorageCreated is true (external storage succeeded), the method only logs and returns without removing any existing local credentials. The else branch creates a new local credential via recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(), but there's no code to remove previous local credentials when external storage succeeds. This means if a user previously had local recovery codes and then gets new ones stored externally, the old local codes would still exist and could potentially be used through the fallback mechanism in RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() which checks federated credentials first, then falls back to local storage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 validates recovery codes without persisting consumption, allowing indefinite replay and incorrectly reporting all codes as remaining. Persist consumption and test replay rejection.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java lines 283-305, the isValid method for recovery codes only checks if the input code exists in the stored list (generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))) but never removes or marks the code as consumed. This means the same recovery code can be used multiple times indefinitely, which is a security vulnerability. Recovery codes are designed to be single-use, so this is a real defect in the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:getCredentials returns a legacy OTP model with unset credentialData and secretData, causing OTP deserialization to fail during account credential listing. Convert it to a modern OTP credential model before returning it.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the getCredentials method in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java (lines 230-248), when myUser.otp is not null, it directly adds myUser.getOtp() to credentialModels without any transformation. The OTP credential stored in MyUser is a basic CredentialModel created in updateCredential (lines 178-189) that only sets type, createdDate, and the raw OTP value - it doesn't set credentialData or secretData fields that modern OTP credential models require. In contrast, the recovery codes are properly converted to RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues() before being added. This inconsistency means when the account REST API tries to deserialize the OTP credential, it will fail because the legacy format lacks the expected structure.
